## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

Coordinate transform:

const VIEW = {w,h,dpr};
let scale, ox, oy;
function resize(){
  dpr = clamp(devicePixelRatio,1,2);
  canvas.width = innerWidth*dpr; canvas.height= innerHeight*dpr;
  canvas.style.width=...
  ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0);
  const portrait = innerWidth < 720 || innerHeight > innerWidth*1.3;
  layout = portrait? PORTRAIT: LANDSCAPE;
  let region = portrait? {x:0, y:65, w:innerWidth, h:innerHeight-65-210} : {x:0,y:0,w:innerWidth,h:innerHeight};
  scale = Math.min(region.w/layout.w, region.h/layout.h);
  ox=region.x+(region.w-layout.w*scale)/2;
  oy=region.y+(region.h-layout.h*scale)/2;
  ...
}
function toWorld(cx,cy){ return {x:(cx-ox)/scale,y:(cy-oy)/scale};}
```

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game based on “Urban battle of clay men with the construction of towers against invasions.”
- Game is implemented as **CLAYFRONT**, a handmade clay-art tower-defense game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; build now and note assumptions briefly when finished.
- Support desktop and mobile with touch controls and responsive layouts.
- Deliver a complete game loop: build towers, defend a core, fight waves, win/lose, restart.

## Decisions
- Built a no-dependency Canvas 2D game with ES modules and static hosting; no build step.
- Theme: clay diorama city under siege; player protects a “Clay Heart” from clay invaders.
- Gameplay: 4 tower types, 2 targeted/instant powers, 10 waves, boss on wave 10, upgrades, selling, early-wave bonuses, pause, speed toggle, sound, persistent best-run record.
- Responsive map layouts: landscape `1280x800`, portrait `720x1000`; both now have 12 build pads so pad indices survive orientation changes.
- Local fonts: Titan One for display, Nunito for UI.
- Layout orientation is chosen by aspect ratio (`innerHeight / innerWidth > 1.15`), not raw width.
- Kept the `window.__clayfront` debug API for QA; may gate behind `?debug=1` or remove before delivery.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full HTML/CSS UI: menu, HUD, dock, tower inspector, instructions, pause, victory/defeat overlays.
- Canvas systems: waves, combat, abilities, particles, projectiles, upgrades, selling, sound synth, responsive scaling.
- Static clay city board, towers, enemies, core heart, pads, rifts, and effects.
- Fixed crash where `rr` was used but not imported in `js/art-enemies.js`; this previously froze the game on the first damaged enemy.
- Fixed inspector never appearing because `.hidden` was never removed.
- Removed default tower preselection to avoid the first Spitter click deselecting it.
- Reworked dock to a single-row layout on wide screens; added compact short-landscape HUD/dock so all pads stay visible/clickable.
- Added short-landscape board lift (`view.oy - 20`) and increased pad tap tolerance (`padRadius + 16`).
- Added portrait pads 10/11 to match landscape pad indices and prevent floating towers on rotation.
- Added data-URI favicon; eliminates prior 404s.
- Visibility-change pause now shows the pause overlay when returning.
- Removed CSS `backdrop-filter` from gameplay panels; headless software FPS improved from ~19.7 to ~31.9 with no meaningful visual loss.
- Tuned balance: slinger range 205, mortar 230, goo 175, kiln 265; landscape pad0 moved to `(1085,270)`; enemy HP scale `1 + waveIndex * .12`; boss scale `1.16 + waveIndex * .05`; boss base HP 4200.
- Automated smoke test passes **30/30** across build, waves, pause, help, abilities, inspector, upgrade/sell, mobile tap-build, defeat, restart, and console errors.
- Responsive automation passes on 10 viewports (360x740 through 1440x900, including 568x320 landscape); all pads visible/clickable and touch-build works.
- Balance simulations: 4 Spitters/no upgrades dies wave 6; 6 Spitters level 2 dies wave 9; 8 Spitters level 3 wins with core 12; 12 maxed Spitters wins core 20; mixed tower strategy wins core 19.
- Captured screenshots including desktop menu/gameplay, inspector, mixed towers, boss, victory, defeat, and mobile portrait/landscape.

### Active
- Final verification after the latest portrait 12-pad change.
- Final screenshot cleanup and possible gating/removal of the debug API.
- Remaining flow checks: pause restart/quit, menu how-to, mobile menu composition.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Rerun smoke and responsive tests after the portrait pad-count change.
2. Inspect portrait screenshot with 12 pads and small-landscape/menu visuals.
3. Test pause restart, quit-to-menu, and menu HOW TO PLAY flows.
4. Decide whether to gate `window.__clayfront` behind `?debug=1` or remove it.
5. Trim intermediate screenshots, keep a small final set, and verify syntax/console cleanliness.
6. Summarize assumptions and deliver.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: game state, waves, combat, input, HUD, debug API, resize/layout logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/util.js`: tower/enemy/wave definitions, ranges, both map layouts, pad positions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page structure, HUD, dock, overlays, favicon.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full responsive clay UI, compact short-landscape HUD/dock.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art-world.js`: table, board, roads, buildings, pads, core, rifts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art-towers.js`: tower sprites/icons.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art-enemies.js`: enemy sprites; now imports `rr`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art-fx.js`: projectiles, effects, particles, floating text.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/fonts/`: local fonts and OFL licenses.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: QA captures; trim to final set.
- `/tmp/opencode/smoke.cjs`: desktop/mobile smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/responsive.cjs`: 10-viewport touch/responsiveness test.
- `/tmp/opencode/balance.cjs` and `/tmp/opencode/balance2.cjs`: balance simulations.
- `/tmp/opencode/victory.cjs`: fast-forward victory capture.

## Important Context
- Dev server is running in tmux session `clayfront` on `http://localhost:3002`; `playwright-cli` session is `clay`.
- Playwright core is at `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/node_modules/playwright-core`; Chromium executable is `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome`.
- `window.__clayfront` exposes `start()`, `menu()`, `startWave()`, `place(type,pad)`, `setClay(n)`, `addClay(n)`, `spawn(type,lane)`, `damageCore(n)`, `skipPrep()`, `fastForward(seconds)`, `quake()`, `rally()`, `speed(n)`, `select(type)`, `upgrade(pad)`, `stateSnapshot()`.
- `fastForward` sets `fastForwarding` to skip `updateHUD` during simulation.
- Tower types: `slinger`, `mortar`, `goo`, `kiln`; enemy types: `runt`, `runner`, `brute`, `splitter`, `boss`.
- Both layouts now have 12 pads; landscape pad0 is `(1085,270)`, portrait pads 10/11 are `(270,690)` and `(450,690)`.
- Headless performance is software-rendered (SwiftShader), so reported FPS is much lower than real GPU browsers; canvas-only baseline was ~32 FPS at 1440x900.
- Working tree is uncommitted; no commit or push has been performed.
- Only remaining console noise previously came from the favicon 404, now fixed; latest tests show zero page errors.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## CLAYFRONT

A handmade clay-art tower defense game for desktop and mobile. The last city is under siege, and its Clay Heart has 20 beats left. Build on the cracked pads, hold both avenues, and survive ten invasion waves.

### Play

No build step or dependencies. Serve the folder over HTTP and open the page:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# then open http://localhost:3002/
```

`start.sh` can also launch the project through the OMGithub runtime.

### Controls

- **Mouse / touch:** pick a tower card, then tap a construction pad. Tap a built tower to inspect, upgrade, or sell it.
- **Keyboard:** `1`–`4` select towers, `Q` targets Clayquake, `E` casts Kiln Rally, `Space` calls the next wave early, `Esc` pauses or cancels targeting, `P` pauses.
- **Powers:** Clayquake stuns and damages a street area; Kiln Rally supercharges every tower for a few seconds.
- **Goal:** survive all 10 waves. Calling waves early grants bonus clay. A boss closes the siege on wave 10.

Progress, sound preference, and the best run are stored locally. The responsive board switches between landscape and portrait layouts, with the same 12 pad positions in both orientations.

### Project layout

- `index.html` — HUD, dock, overlays, and dialogs.
- `styles.css` — responsive clay UI and safe-area/landscape layouts.
- `js/game.js` — game loop, waves, combat, input, powers, and persistence.
- `js/util.js` — tower/enemy definitions, waves, and map geometry.
- `js/art-*.js` — procedural canvas art for the city, towers, invaders, and effects.
- `assets/fonts/` — locally hosted display/UI fonts with licenses.

`window.__clayfront` exposes a small development/QA API in the browser console. It is safe to ignore during normal play.

+
+## CLAYFRONT
+
+A handmade clay-art tower defense game for desktop and mobile. The last city is under siege, and its Clay Heart has 20 beats left. Build on the cracked pads, hold both avenues, and survive ten invasion waves.
+
+### Play
+
+No build step or dependencies. Serve the folder over HTTP and open the page:
+
+```bash
+python3 -m http.server 3002
+# then open http://localhost:3002/
+```
+
+`start.sh` can also launch the project through the OMGithub runtime.
+
+### Controls
+
+- **Mouse / touch:** pick a tower card, then tap a construction pad. Tap a built tower to inspect, upgrade, or sell it.
+- **Keyboard:** `1`–`4` select towers, `Q` targets Clayquake, `E` casts Kiln Rally, `Space` calls the next wave early, `Esc` pauses or cancels targeting, `P` pauses.
+- **Powers:** Clayquake stuns and damages a street area; Kiln Rally supercharges every tower for a few seconds.
+- **Goal:** survive all 10 waves. Calling waves early grants bonus clay. A boss closes the siege on wave 10.
+
+Progress, sound preference, and the best run are stored locally. The responsive board switches between landscape and portrait layouts, with the same 12 pad positions in both orientations.
+
+### Project layout
+
+- `index.html` — HUD, dock, overlays, and dialogs.
+- `styles.css` — responsive clay UI and safe-area/landscape layouts.
+- `js/game.js` — game loop, waves, combat, input, powers, and persistence.
+- `js/util.js` — tower/enemy definitions, waves, and map geometry.
+- `js/art-*.js` — procedural canvas art for the city, towers, invaders, and effects.
+- `assets/fonts/` — locally hosted display/UI fonts with licenses.
+
+`window.__clayfront` exposes a small development/QA API in the browser console. It is safe to ignore during normal play.
+
